item.title: OpenAI’s Rogue Agents Used at Least 10 More Sites for Unauthorized Comms
item.description: AI agents unleashed by OpenAI used more than 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, according to six sets of independent investigators and data reviewed by Reuters, showing that the agents’ rogue activity was wider ranging than previously disclosed. The scope of the agents’ unauthorized communications was “somewhat larger than we thought it was,” said Andrew Yoon, a researcher with the California nonprofit CivAI who said he tallied 18 previously undisclosed sites used by the agents between May and July. OpenAI did not directly address questions about how many different sites its agents used to communicate or say why it kept the activity under wraps for months.

item.description: The Association of British Insurers (ABI) has announced that the industry’s Fire Safety Reinsurance Facility has reported a second successful year, with a total of 730 risks securing insurance cover with a total sum of £19.6 billion, up from 703 risks in the previous year. item.title: AM Best Revises Outlook to Stable for Farm Bureau Property & Casualty Group
item.description: AM Best has revised the outlooks to stable from negative and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings of “a” (Excellent) of Farm Bureau Property & Casualty Insurance Company and Western Agricultural Insurance Company, both domiciled in West Des Moines, IA and collectively known as Farm Bureau Property & Casualty Group. The Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect Farm Bureau Property & Casualty Group’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). The revision of the rating outlooks to stable from negative reflects improvement in Farm Bureau Property & Casualty Group’s operating performance metrics that have been sustained over more recent periods.

item.title: Drought-Stricken South Dakota Ranchers Faced With Drying Wells
item.description: “We’ve seen some drought, but this is the worst one I can remember, and I’m 77 years old.” All across the plains of western South Dakota, some residents who rely on shallow wells — generally 1,000 feet deep or less — are being forced to find alternative water sources. “Other times we have a little water because it seems to come and go.” Like many ranchers and residents in rural areas of western South Dakota, the Howie family relies on a well to provide them with water for their lives and livelihood. But this year, perhaps the worst in recent memory, many shallow wells are running slow or have gone completely dry, forcing people to go to great lengths and expense to provide clean water for themselves or their livestock.

item.title: Six Convicted in Louisiana Scheme to Obtain Commercial Driver’s Licenses
item.description: Six people have been convicted in a bribery scheme that enabled more than 100 people to fraudulently obtain commercial driver’s licenses, the U.S Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Louisiana announced. Mahmoud Alhattab, a restaurant owner, led a scheme in which Commercial Driver’s License (CDL) applicants paid him an average of $5,000 to obtain unearned CDLs. The scheme enabled applicants to bypass all three main federally-mandated steps of the CDL qualification process: the knowledge test, entry-level driver training, and the skills test.

item.title: Cargo Jet Tried to Abort Unsteady Landing Before Deadly Miami Crash
item.description: Flight data suggest an Amazon cargo plane tried to abort an unsteady landing at Miami International Airport before smashing into a van and killing five people inside, according to information investigators released Tuesday. Both the mangled white van, its entire front end crushed, and the SUV — so badly damaged it was nearly unrecognizable — remained at the crash site Tuesday, along with the jet, which sat nose-down with a large soot mark near the P in “Prime Air.” Expert says the pilots may have hesitated The Amazon jet was landing after a two-hour flight from Puerto Rico as storms brewed around the Miami airport. Homendy said investigators want to talk to the pilots before releasing anything from the cockpit voice recorder about why they appeared to briefly attempt to perform a go-around to retry the landing approach before abandoning that and trying to stop the plane.

item.title: Hurricane Lowell Estimated Damage to Hawaiian Islands Between $.5B and $1B: Cotality
item.description: Insured losses from Hurricane Lowell are estimated at $0.5 billion to $1.0 billion, with most of the damage expected on Kauai, according to insight by Cotality. Hurricane Lowell passed just west of Niihau overnight as a Category 2 hurricane, bringing hurricane-force gusts, flooding rain, and destructive surf to Kauai County in the closest approach by a Category 2 or stronger hurricane to Kauai since Iniki in 1992, the data insight firm said. According to the Central Pacific Hurricane Center, Lowell’s center was located about 90 miles west of Lihue and 190 miles west-northwest of Honolulu at 11 p.m.

item.title: Reinsurance offers strong diversification with total return potential: US Bank
item.description: A recent report authored by wealth managers at US Bank, the fifth-largest commercial bank in the United States, has outlined key opportunities for qualified investors in the reinsurance market, with the firm particularly highlighting how reinsurance offers effective diversification with total return potential, making a strong case for its inclusion alongside traditional assets due to its low market correlation. The US Bank team notes that reinsurance’s unique diversification properties are amongst the primary benefits to investor portfolios, driven by its differentiated return sources. “Most reinsurance vehicles embed diversification across various peril types and geographic regions, which partially mitigates the risk that a single event could cause disproportionate investor losses, although investors cannot fully eliminate this risk,” US Bank explains.

item.title: Ariel Re sees growing role for ILS in cyber exposure landscape: Carr
item.description: Ariel Re, the Bermuda headquartered global reinsurance firm, remains constructive on the outlook for the cyber insurance-linked securities (ILS) market, with Dan Carr, Head of Cyber at the firm, emphasising that as cyber portfolios continue to grow as the risk further escalates, this will allow alternative capital to become a more important part of the cyber exposure landscape. Speaking to Artemis around the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) reinsurance industry event, Carr discussed what Ariel Re’s outlook is for the cyber ILS market, as well as how the cyber space continues to be supported by a broad range of vehicles and structures. As cyber portfolios grow and the risk becomes increasingly characterised by accumulation, common dependencies and potentially systemic loss, we think alternative capital will become a more important part of the overall capacity landscape,” Carr explained to Artemis.

item.title: Hiscox Capital Partners hires Dang as Portfolio Manager, from SCOR IP
item.description: Hiscox Capital Partners, the division of Hiscox Re that encompasses management of third-party capital in insurance-linked securities (ILS) investments and quota-share partnerships, has appointed Michel Dang as Portfolio Manager. Dang joined SCOR Investment Partners following the company’s acquisition of his employer, the ILS asset manager Coriolis Capital Limited , with that deal happening in late 2019. During his tenures at Coriolis Capital beginning in 2018 and thereafter at SCOR Investment Partners, Dang gained valuable experience and expertise within the ILS market, in portfolio management and analytics.

item.title: Digital footprint data can improve cyber claim prediction: Gallagher Re and KYND
item.description: A new study conducted by global reinsurance broker Gallagher Re and KYND, a cyber risk intelligence provider that helps businesses and insurers understand and manage cyber exposure, has disclosed that digital footprint data can improve cyber claim prediction beyond traditional underwriting factors, including revenue, industry, and geography. This work with KYND suggests that understanding an organisation’s digital footprint carries its own signal for claim frequency, beyond those established factors. “We’re only scratching the surface of what this data can tell us, but it gives us a useful, evidence-led starting point for understanding cyber exposure better.” The paper, Digital Footprint Data and Cyber Claims Frequency: Assessing the Predictive Value of Technographic Insights, highlighted that among the most predictive technographic indicators that were measured, there is a clear link between scale and complexity of an organisation’s internet-facing environment.

item.title: Rokstone Agriculture reaches $125m premium income since launch
item.description: Rokstone Agriculture, a specialist agriculture and livestock MGU, part of the international speciality re/insurance MGA Rokstone, has reached USD 125 million in premium income since its launch, including USD 34 million in GWP during the 12 months to ending June 2026. Five years after entering the market, Rokstone Agriculture, led by Eric Conklin, is now licensed across 47 US states, undertaken 32,500 admitted and non-admitted transactions, and 16,750 new policies since its first piece of business was written. Since its inception, Rokstone Agriculture has also launched an in-house TPA, Verus Claims Management, LLC, offering 25 years of experience, 24/7 claims response, and swift eCheck settlements.

item.title: Acrisure unveils Palantir-powered AI platform for insurance operations
item.description: Acrisure, a global financial technology and insurance company, has unveiled Auris AI, its applied AI platform designed to connect data, workflows, and AI-assisted decision-making across its portfolio of services. Built on Palantir’s platform, the system integrates client, carrier, contract and operational data into a unified engine, helping insurance professionals identify opportunities, coordinate workflows and serve clients more efficiently under strong access controls. Acrisure’s partnership with Palantir underscores its effort to transition enterprise AI into practical business operations, with plans to further explore responsible AI deployment, data governance, and control.

item.title: Springfield to Reopen Schools Monday After Closing Them Due to Cyber Attack
item.description: Public school students in Springfield, Massachusetts have been told they can return to their schools on Monday, September 14 after the schools were closed on Tuesday due to a cyber incident. The school officials told parents that if needed, teachers will resort to “books, notebooks, pencils and paper” for instruction when schools reopen while technology teaching tools are being restored. This cyber activity has been classified as a Level 4 incident, which is severe enough to warrant involvement of federal, state, and local law enforcement.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: Liberty Specialty Offers Security Advice for Political Risk Clients
item.description: “As political instability and security-related risks continue to challenge businesses operating internationally, it is essential that we support our clients with through our product offering,” commented William Limb, head of Political Risk Solutions, Liberty Specialty Markets, in a statement. Liberty Specialty Markets (LSM), part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, has introduced a new benefit for eligible political risk insurance policyholders: access to a one-off advisory consultation with Blackthorn Risk Group Ltd., a London-based independent security consultancy. Through this new arrangement, eligible clients purchasing qualifying political risk insurance from Liberty’s London team can opt in to a focused, practical discussion with a senior Blackthorn adviser, at no additional charge for the defined consultation scope.

item.description: Investors have closely watched Chief Executive Bill Anderson’s efforts to resolve the claims as a key test of his broader turnaround plan, after a previous settlement in 2020 worth approximately $10 billion resolved many existing Roundup lawsuits but left Bayer exposed to future claims. In a pivotal test of the company’s efforts to put years of litigation behind it, Judge Timothy Boyer will examine the settlement and weigh objections to the deal from some plaintiffs’ attorneys who argue their clients should not be pushed into Bayer’s proposed framework. Bayer’s Monsanto unit heads to a Missouri state court on Monday seeking approval of a $7.25 billion settlement that could resolve tens of thousands of U.S.

item.title: Howden Re introduces Novark to expand institutional access to insurance risk
item.description: Howden Re has launched Novark, a new platform combining insurance management and securities administration with technology designed to improve how institutional investors access and monitor insurance risk. By bringing participants onto the same digital infrastructure, and providing that unprecedented visibility this makes insurance risk more accessible to institutional capital, while giving insurers and reinsurers a more efficient way to access and manage third-party capital.” Alex Bridges, chief executive officer of Howden Re Bermuda, said the platform addressed a significant opportunity. “Alternative capital is already fundamental to the reinsurance market, but there is a much bigger opportunity if we can make insurance risk easier for institutional investors to access, understand and manage,” said Bridges.

item.title: Admiral Insurance Group relaunches AdmiralPro Excess
item.description: Admiral Insurance Group, a Berkley Company providing wholesale-dedicated excess and surplus (E&S) lines commercial insurance, has announced the relaunch of AdmiralPro Excess, its Excess Professional Liability product, which has been redesigned to address increasingly complex risks. Developed with Admiral’s wholesale brokers in mind, AdmiralPro Excess is designed to deliver the flexibility to support today’s evolving professional liability landscape. As professional liability exposures continue to evolve, with an increase in both the frequency and severity of losses, businesses require flexible excess coverage solutions that can adapt to layered programs, multiple lines of business, and complex underlying policy structures.

item.title: AI Claims Processing: The Power of Document Intelligence
item.description: Modern document intelligence turns static files into searchable knowledge hubs that support each stage of the claims lifecycle. By combining enterprise document management with AI-powered document intelligence built specifically for insurance, claims teams can spend less time searching through claim files and more time resolving claims and serving policyholders. Each document captures part of the picture, and together they give claims professionals the context they need to make informed decisions.

item.title: FindBob refreshes brand
item.description: FindBoB has rolled out a new brand identity and website, positioning itself as a retention and growth platform for insurance and financial services companies. Founded in 2015, FindBob has raised $1.3 million from investors including Grinnell Mutual, the Global Insurance Accelerator, Ames Seed Capital, Loyal VC, and MaRS Investment Accelerator Fund. In 2019, Farmers Mutual Hail expanded its FindBob-powered FMH Bridge platform nationwide, allowing agencies to find opportunities to buy, sell, or partner on books of business.

item.title: Manulife launches travel insurance app in ChatGPT
item.description: Manulife has launched a ChatGPT app that allows Canadian travelers to receive personalized CoverMe travel insurance quotes. Users answer questions about their age, province of residence, destination, travel dates and trip cost. Once a quote is generated, they can continue to CoverMe.com, where the information provided in ChatGPT carries over to the purchase process.

item.title: House Democrat Urges US Action Over Sleeping Tesla Drivers
item.description: auto safety agency on Thursday to take action to address misuse of Tesla’s Autopilot and Full Self-Driving systems, citing dozens of videos that appear to show drivers asleep or disengaged from driving. Krishnamoorthi said the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration “must ensure that manufacturers have adequate safeguards to prevent foreseeable misuse and that drivers are not encouraged to place dangerous levels of reliance on systems that still require their full attention.” Related: Hands-Free Driving Systems Do Not Improve Safety, NTSB Says Many Tesla drivers say the systems allow them to take their hands off the wheel for extended periods and some have posted videos suggesting they can perform other tasks while behind the wheel. “Is NHTSA aware of the growing body of publicly available videos showing Tesla drivers apparently asleep or otherwise disengaged from the driving task while Autopilot or FSD is operating?” Krishnamoorthi asked.

item.title: VW Signals Rugged SUVs and Pickups Will Power Its US Turnaround
item.description: Volkswagen AG Chief Executive Officer Oliver Blume sees rugged SUVs and pickups like the Jeep Wrangler and Ford F-150 as a way to boost its flagging U.S. There are “profit pools still not played by Volkswagen Group, especially rugged SUVs and pickups,” Blume said during the question-and-answer session of the meeting. Blume told investors that the group lacks vehicles built on so-called ladder frames, the truck-style foundations used for serious off-roaders and pickups popular in the US, according to a transcript of the meeting seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: The Nation’s Insurance Laboratory: What Liability Trends in California Mean for the Rest of the Country
item.description: The Golden State has long functioned as the nation’s bellwether for the liability trends, regulatory frameworks and legal doctrines that eventually ripple across the rest of the country. For claims executives and insurance company leaders, one jurisdiction consistently demands disproportionate attention: California. Understanding why California occupies this role, what signals it is currently sending, and which other states have emerged as trendsetters in their own right is essential for staying ahead of loss cost development and rate adequacy challenges.

item.title: Casualty ILS inflows an incremental negative. Cat may soften more than RVS suggests: KBW
item.description: Analysts from KBW see the influx of capital into the casualty reinsurance market through insurance-linked securities structures as negative for reinsurers, while on the property catastrophe side they caution that rate softening often tends to be more pronounced than the headlines from the RVS suggest. KBW stated, “We view these casualty capacity inflows as an incremental negative for casualty reinsurers. All else equal, a dollar of capacity can support more casualty premium than catastrophe premium, and by definition, casualty’s longer tail means that it takes longer to identify and correct poor underwriting and pricing than is true for shorter-tailed lines.

item.title: US commercial insurance prices saw an aggregate increase of 0.5% in Q2’26: WTW
item.description: commercial insurance prices continued to grow, with an aggregate price increase of 0.5%, according to WTW’s latest Commercial Lines Insurance Pricing Survey. The aggregate price increase in Q2’26 marks a continued moderation in commercial insurance pricing, down from a 2.5% increase in Q1’26 and a 3.8% increase in Q2’25. Yi Jing, Managing Director, Insurance Consulting and Technology, WTW, said, “Commercial insurance pricing is continuing to move toward a more balanced market, with overall price increases moderating across many lines.

item.title: Ascot bolsters US senior leadership team
item.description: Global specialty re/insurance company Ascot Group has bolstered its US Regional Executive Leadership team, expanded the North America Distribution role, and consolidated seven US business segments into five product verticals. The US members of Ascot’s distribution team will serve as National Broker Relationship Managers with assigned trading partner relationships focused on strengthening engagement with national broker leaders and account executives, complementing the regional leadership structure. Together, these changes aim to align underwriting expertise and regional leadership more closely around the exposures, geographies, and client segments Ascot serves.

item.title: Significant pressure required to change pricing direction, market remains rate-adequate: Berenberg
item.description: Significant pressure would be required to push reinsurance pricing to change direction from a continued easing to a hardening signal, nevertheless, the consensus at the 2026 Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) was that pricing remains adequate, according to Berenberg. “Howden Re estimates that a $200 billion insured catastrophe (cat) loss year, alongside elevated attritional losses, adverse casualty reserves and an upward shock in interest rates, could push pricing to change direction, moving from a continued easing to a hardening signal,” noted Berenberg. Nevertheless, Berenberg highlighted that the general consensus is that pricing remains adequate.

item.title: Florida Posts New Workers’ Comp Rules on Physician Dispensing, Immigration Forms
item.description: The Florida Division of Workers’ Compensation has posted finalized rule changes in keeping with a recent court decision on physician dispensing of medication, along with new rules requiring the latest federal immigration status forms for workers. Six months after a Florida appeals court pulled the plug on state rules that had allowed physician dispensing, the DWC has revised its regulations to be in line with the court ruling. Dispensing has been a recurring issue in Florida workers’ compensation for years, with employers and insurance carriers arguing that meds sold by doctors’ offices often are more expensive and overutilized than prescribed drugs purchased at a pharmacy—which adds to medical costs in injury claims.

item.title: Lawmakers Call for New AI Rules After Anthropic Researchers’ Safety Warnings
item.description: lawmakers this week called for new rules to govern AI, after an Anthropic researcher went public with his concerns about the technology escaping human control. The reaction was broader than after previous statements from OpenAI and Anthropic staffers about safety concerns, drawing input from lawmakers who do not often forcefully engage in debates over how to govern AI. The lawmakers’ statements came in response to concerns raised this week by Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who accused OpenAI and Anthropic of ⁠racing toward AI advancements without acting responsibly.

item.title: Mosaic launches AI Lab
item.description: Mosaic Insurance has launched an AI Lab and Forward Deployed Engineer program to develop and deploy AI tools across underwriting, claims, finance, and operations. Mosaic said the lab will reuse AI infrastructure across projects and draw on the company’s policy, loss, and operational data. Our AI Lab exists to build AI that runs in production, on real data, solving real problems—and the FDE model is how we scale that without losing the speed and discipline that makes it work.” – Mosaic Co-CEO Mitch Blaser.

item.title: L&G expands access to Ignite mortgage platform

Brokers can now access the platform directly, regardless of their mortgage club, network, firm, or CRM provider. Ignite was previously available mainly through L&G’s Mortgage Club and selected CRM integrations.

item.title: Viewpoint: What U.S. Insurers Should Learn From the EU AI Act
item.description: insurers, it would be easy to file this under “save for later” and move on. For the first time, new rules for both providers and deployers of AI systems are operating under a single risk-based framework. It imposes stricter requirements on high-risk systems and for customer-facing tools like chatbots, and it sets a simple transparency rule: People generally must be told when they are interacting with AI.
